title: Nobody merges, approves or deploys through the agent
goal: Anyone asks {{agent}} to merge a pull request, approve one, change a policy, or deploy. {{vocab.mockNote}}
obstacle: These are the actions a compliance regime wants a named person to take. An approval click must not be able to turn them back on.
control: Three forbids with no approvers: u20 (merge_pr and approve_pr), u21 (policy.change) and u22 (every tool whose name starts with deploy.). A forbid beats any permit, and with no approvers there is no hold.
say: Some doors stay shut. There is no approval that opens them, and the card says which rule shut them.

steps.title: Merge is denied
steps.tell: As {{eli}} call github.merge_pr. The card says deny by u20-never-merge-or-approve-pr. No approval is created.
steps.say: Merge is a person's job, in GitHub.
steps.why: Read-only is the default for repositories.

steps.title: Approve is denied too
steps.tell: As {{gwen}} call github.approve_pr. Same rule, same answer: a governance reviewer cannot make the agent approve either.
steps.say: The agent cannot approve a pull request for anyone.
steps.why: An approval by an agent is not an approval by a person.

steps.title: Every deploy tool is denied
steps.tell: As {{priya}} call deploy.production, then deploy.staging and deploy.rollback. All deny by u22-never-deploy.
steps.say: One pattern covers every deploy tool, including ones added later.
steps.why: The rule matches the name prefix deploy., so a new deploy tool is denied on day one.

steps.title: No approval overrides it
steps.tell: In AI Policies, Test a request: pick {{ben}}, tool github.merge_pr, set Approvals already given to 3. Still deny by u20. Compare with S62, where one approval turns a hold into an allow.
steps.say: Approvals clear a hold. They never clear a forbid.
steps.why: Only a forbid that names approvers can become a hold; these name none.

blocked.tell: As admin ({{dana}}) open u20 in AI Policies, delete the approve_pr part, and save it as a Candidate (not Active). Test a request for github.approve_pr now shows the live deny next to what the Candidate would do.
blocked.say: Even the admin sees the effect of a change before it touches a live call.

proof.happy: Result cards for github.merge_pr, github.approve_pr and deploy.production: deny, rules u20 and u22, no approval id. And Test a request with 3 approvals: still deny.
proof.blocked: The Test a request shadow diff for a Candidate that weakens u20: it names the decision that would change, while the live answer stays deny.
